solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Greek leader's misdeed — nothing changed

indicators.note: changed tells us the letters of the misdeed plus a zero are to be rearranged

parts.note: nothing is zero, the round letter O

explanation.surface: A Greek commander's wrongdoing, with nothing about it altered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed' shuffles MISDEED plus O. Diomedes is a Greek leader in Troilus and Cressida.
explanation.definitionFit: Diomedes is one of the Greek commanders at the siege of Troy, appearing in Shakespeare's Troilus and Cressida.

clue.text: Dead whales for shepherdess

parts.note: orcas are killer whales

explanation.surface: Dead whales exchanged for a girl who tends sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: Dorcas is a shepherdess in the sheep-shearing scene of The Winter's Tale.

clue.text: Mature hock in northern town

parts.note: mature means old
hock is a cut of meat from the leg, ham

explanation.surface: Aged German white wine in a town up north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hock' looks like the German wine but is the joint of meat. OLDHAM is a town near Manchester in North West England.
explanation.definitionFit: Oldham is a former mill town in Greater Manchester, in the north of England.

clue.text: Lofty dwelling that's strangely frightening, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly signals that a word with the same sound is wanted

parts.note: strangely frightening means eerie

explanation.surface: A tall home with a spooky feel, so people say.
explanation.definitionFit: An eagle's nest, built high on a crag, is a lofty home.

clue.text: Drivers seen in smash, holding drink

indicators.note: holding says the rearranged letters contain the drink
smash suggests breaking the word seen up and reassembling it

parts.note: gin is a drink

explanation.surface: Motorists spotted in a crash, still clutching a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drivers' reads as motorists, matching the crash in the surface, but here means machines that drive things; 'smash' is the anagram signal, not the accident.
explanation.definitionFit: Engines are the machines that power and drive vehicles.

clue.text: Lord knocks back inferior cider and scrumpy for starters

indicators.note: knocks back, like downing a drink, signals that the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: inferior means poor

indicators.note: for starters asks for the opening letter of each of the two drinks

explanation.surface: A nobleman downs cheap cider and scrumpy to begin with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocks back' reverses POOR followed by C and S. Scrumpy is rough farmhouse cider from the West of England. Lord Scroop is a traitor in Henry V.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord Scroop is a nobleman in Henry V, executed for plotting against the king.

clue.text: Heartless Capulet or a devious Queen

indicators.note: devious signals that the letters are twisted into a new order
heartless says the central letter of Capulet is removed

explanation.surface: A cruel Capulet, or perhaps a scheming queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' drops the middle U of CAPULET, leaving CAPLET; 'devious' shuffles that with OR A.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleopatra is the Egyptian queen of Antony and Cleopatra.

clue.text: Allowance gien in big discoursess

indicators.note: in says the allowance is placed inside the abbreviation for big

parts.note: OS, outsize, is the clothing abbreviation for big
a ration is a fixed allowance

explanation.surface: A quota handed out during long-winded speeches.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue as printed has typos: 'gien' for given and 'discoursess' for discourses.
explanation.definitionFit: Orations are formal speeches, discourses delivered to an audience.

clue.text: Excuse bound to be a source of gratification

parts.note: a plea is an excuse offered
bound to, as in certain to, means sure

explanation.surface: A pretext that is certain to give satisfaction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound' means certain here (sure to), not tied up or leaping.
explanation.definitionFit: Enjoyment or delight is what gratifies, so pleasure is a source of gratification.

clue.text: Venetian gentleman travelled with Stravinsky, cycling

parts.note: travelled, as on horseback, means rode

indicators.note: cycling says the letters of the composer's first name go round, the last moving to the front

parts.note: Igor Stravinsky, the composer

explanation.surface: A man from Venice went on a bike ride with the composer Stravinsky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycling' moves the R of IGOR to the front, giving RIGO. Roderigo is the dupe of Iago in Othello.
explanation.definitionFit: Roderigo is a Venetian gentleman in Othello, manipulated by Iago.

clue.text: Tom East's weird sister

parts.note: a tom is a male cat, a he-cat

explanation.surface: Tom East's strange sibling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tom East' reads like a person's name, but a tom is a he-cat.
explanation.definitionFit: Hecate is the goddess of witchcraft who leads the witches, the weird sisters, in Macbeth.

clue.text: Records of events lost pounds and shillings — and this

indicators.note: lost signals the money letters are taken away

parts.note: annals are yearly records of events

explanation.surface: Historical records that dropped the money columns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this' is defined by its company: like pounds and shillings, an anna is a coin, a former Indian one worth a sixteenth of a rupee. Shillings are old British coins.
explanation.definitionFit: Grouped with pounds and shillings, the word means another currency unit, the old Indian coin.

clue.text: A courageous military leader — not French — Greek

parts.note: game means willing and courageous

indicators.note: leader asks for the first letter of the word military

parts.note: non is French for not

explanation.surface: A brave army commander, not French but Greek.
explanation.walkthrough: Agamemnon is the Greek commander-in-chief in Troilus and Cressida.
explanation.definitionFit: Agamemnon, King of Mycenae, led the Greek forces against Troy.

clue.text: Eastcheap rogue cuts half the garden flower

indicators.note: cuts half the says only the first half of the flower's name is kept

parts.note: the poinsettia is a red-bracted flowering plant

explanation.surface: A tavern villain chops down half the flowers in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: POINSETTIA has ten letters; keeping the first five gives the answer. Eastcheap is the London street of the Boar's Head tavern in Henry IV.
explanation.definitionFit: Poins is Prince Hal's roguish companion among the Eastcheap tavern crowd in Henry IV.

clue.text: Dress returned to 6 down's attendant

indicators.note: returned says the garment's letters are read backwards

parts.note: a sari is an Indian dress

explanation.surface: A frock sent back to the queen's lady-in-waiting.
explanation.definitionFit: Iras is one of the waiting-women of Cleopatra, the 6 down solution, in Antony and Cleopatra.

clue.text: Launched — the carpet?

definitions.meaning: launched as a product or service is introduced to the market
a red carpet is unrolled for an occasion

explanation.definitionFit: A product launch is described as being unrolled to the public, and a carpet is unrolled along the floor.

clue.text: A new singer for Trojan commander

parts.note: a tenor is a male singer

explanation.surface: A fresh vocalist cast as a Trojan general.
explanation.definitionFit: Antenor is one of the Trojan commanders in Troilus and Cressida.

clue.text: Revised screed about feminine middleman causes signs of embarrassment

indicators.note: about says the rearranged letters go around the other pieces
revised signals that the letters of screed are reworked

parts.note: read as middle of man, the central letter of that word

explanation.surface: A rewritten rant about a female go-between leads to blushes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revised' shuffles SCREED into REDCES and 'about' wraps it round F and A. 'middleman' looks like a broker but means the middle letter of MAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Blushing faces, flushed scarlet, are what people show when embarrassed.

clue.text: Tenant upset company trophy. That is right

indicators.note: upset, in a down clue, turns the company abbreviation upside down

parts.note: a cup is a trophy
i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A resident knocks over a firm's trophy, and that's fair enough.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenant is someone who occupies a property, holding it as resident.

clue.text: Clauses rewritten for Italian prince

indicators.note: rewritten signals that the letters of clauses are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Contract clauses redrafted for an Italian royal.
explanation.definitionFit: Escalus is the Prince of Verona in Romeo and Juliet.

clue.text: Fire and pillage

definitions.meaning: to fire is to dismiss from a job
to pillage is to plunder a captured town

explanation.definitionFit: Both dismissal from employment and the plundering of a captured city share the same short word.

clue.text: Royal castle. Arundel? In part

indicators.note: In part says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Arundel Castle in Sussex, home of a royal-blooded duke, glimpsed in part.
explanation.definitionFit: King Lear is Shakespeare's royal tragic hero, a king of ancient Britain.

clue.text: Fruit drink — one of honey — in lounge

indicators.note: in says the honey drink goes within the word for lounge

parts.note: to lie is to lounge about
mead is a drink made of honey

explanation.surface: A fruity beverage, one with honey, served in a living room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lounge' looks like a room but is a verb, to lie about; 'one of honey' is a drink made of honey.
explanation.definitionFit: Limeade is a soft drink flavoured with lime juice.

clue.text: Shrew's sister could be the studio presenter on the radio

indicators.note: on the radio signals a word heard rather than seen

parts.note: to be the studio presenter is to be anchor of a programme

explanation.surface: The Shrew's sibling might host the show on air.
explanation.walkthrough: BE ANCHOR said in a non-rhotic British accent matches the name. The Shrew is Katherina in The Taming of the Shrew.
explanation.definitionFit: Bianca is the younger sister of Katherina, the shrew of The Taming of the Shrew.

clue.text: Count disapproves, about to be dropped

indicators.note: to be dropped says the letters for about are removed

parts.note: censures means disapproves of
re is a word for about, concerning

explanation.surface: A nobleman frowns on things, but his concerns are to be set aside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Count' looks like a nobleman but is a head count.
explanation.definitionFit: A census is an official count of a population.

clue.text: Instrument. Loud one

parts.note: F, forte, is the musical marking for loud
one stands for another instrument, here a lute

explanation.surface: A musical instrument, and a noisy one at that.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' refers back to 'Instrument': a lute is one.
explanation.definitionFit: The flute is a woodwind instrument played by blowing across a hole.

clue.text: Award nicely laid out for king

indicators.note: laid out says the letters of nicely are set out afresh, around the honour

parts.note: MBE, Member of the Order of the British Empire, is a British honour

explanation.surface: An honour neatly presented to a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'laid out' rearranges NICELY as CY...LINE with MBE kept whole in the middle. An MBE is an honour awarded by the British monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Cymbeline is the ancient British king who gives his name to Shakespeare's late romance.

clue.text: Eleven hundred spoken of as presenter

indicators.note: spoken of signals that the letters are said out as a word

parts.note: MC is eleven hundred in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: One thousand one hundred mentioned as a host.
explanation.definitionFit: A master of ceremonies hosts and introduces an event, a compere.

clue.text: Tamora's son from Chinese press

parts.note: to press clothes is to iron them

explanation.surface: A queen's son brought from a Chinese printing press.
explanation.definitionFit: Chiron is one of the sons of Tamora, Queen of the Goths, in Titus Andronicus.

clue.text: Roman officer with mother, creating a scene

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother

indicators.note: creating, in the sense of making a fuss, signals the letters of a scene are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A Roman officer whose mum is making a fuss in public.
explanation.walkthrough: 'creating' shuffles A SCENE into ECENAS. Maecenas is a follower of Octavius in Antony and Cleopatra.
explanation.definitionFit: Maecenas appears as a Roman officer serving Octavius Caesar in Antony and Cleopatra.

clue.text: Loyal servant knocking back round confectionery items

indicators.note: knocking back, like downing food, signals the pieces are read in reverse

parts.note: O is a round shape
tarts are sweet pastries

explanation.surface: A faithful servant wolfing down a round of sweet pastries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocking back' reverses O followed by TARTS. Strato is the servant who holds the sword for Brutus in Julius Caesar.
explanation.definitionFit: Strato is Brutus's loyal servant, who helps him die by his own sword in Julius Caesar.

clue.text: Spartan king with workers on English landaus, joiner missing

parts.note: men are workers, a team's staff

indicators.note: missing says the joining word is taken out of landaus

parts.note: and is a joining word, a conjunction

explanation.surface: A Spartan king rides with his staff in English carriages, one hitch missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' takes AND from LANDAUS, leaving LAUS. A landau is a four-wheeled horse-drawn carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Menelaus, King of Sparta, is the husband of Helen in Troilus and Cressida.
